description: How online games keep many players in agreement over an unreliable network: transport choices, state synchronisation, lag compensation, client-side prediction, cheating defences and scalable servers. Students write client and server code, impair simulated links and watch packets, then build a small authoritative multiplayer game.
modelledOn: Stevens, Fenner and Rudoff, UNIX Network Programming, Volume 1
Glazer and Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games
Kurose and Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
outcomes: Choose and justify a client-server or peer-to-peer architecture and tick rate for a given game and network budget.
Implement a reliability layer on UDP with sequence numbers, acknowledgements and channel semantics.
Synchronise game state with snapshots, delta compression, interpolation and interest management.
Reduce perceived latency with client-side prediction, reconciliation and server-side lag compensation, and measure the result under emulated loss and jitter.
Design a server-authoritative protocol that resists common cheats and spoofing.
Plan matchmaking, regional server fleets and capacity for a game with a target concurrent user count and a data-cost limit.

units.title: Networked game architectures
topics: Client-server, listen-server, peer-to-peer and relay architectures compared
The game loop, fixed timestep, tick rates and determinism
The sockets API: UDP and TCP sockets in code and non-blocking I/O
Network budget of a game: packets per second, bandwidth, MTU and fragmentation
Case study: mobile multiplayer on 3G and 4G in Africa, data caps and cost per player

units.title: Transport and reliability
topics: TCP versus UDP for games: head-of-line blocking and Nagle's algorithm
A reliability layer over UDP: sequence numbers, acknowledgement bitfields and retransmission
Channels: reliable ordered, unreliable sequenced and reliable unordered messages
Packet loss, congestion and bandwidth estimation
Serialisation: binary encoding, bit-packing, quantisation and delta compression

units.title: State synchronisation
topics: Lockstep simulation and input delay for strategy games
Snapshot replication: full and delta snapshots and acknowledgement-based baselines
Entity interpolation, extrapolation and dead reckoning
Replicated state versus remote procedure calls and events; priority accumulators
Interest management: area-of-interest filtering and relevancy

units.title: Latency, jitter and lag compensation
topics: Measuring round-trip time, jitter and loss; clock synchronisation between client and server
Interpolation delay and jitter buffers
Server-side lag compensation: rewinding the world for hit detection
Network emulation: delay, loss, duplication and reordering as a test tool
Fairness: peeker's advantage and how tick rate and ping interact

units.title: Client-side prediction and rollback
topics: Predicting local input and reconciling with authoritative server state
Smoothing prediction errors without visible snapping
Rollback netcode with deterministic re-simulation for fighting games
Misprediction with non-deterministic physics and other players' actions

units.title: Cheating, trust and server authority
topics: Server authority: validating every client command
A taxonomy of cheats: speed hacks, aimbots, packet tampering, replay and information leaks
Authentication and encryption: connect tokens, DTLS, spoofing and amplification attacks
Anti-cheat approaches: statistical detection, server-side checks and replay review
Player privacy, data protection and safe play for children

units.title: Matchmaking and scaling game servers
topics: Lobbies and skill-based matchmaking with rating systems (Elo and Glicko style)
Dedicated server fleets: containers, regions and autoscaling
NAT traversal: hole punching with STUN-style discovery and relay fallback
World sharding, instancing and seamless borders for persistent worlds
Persistence: player profiles, leaderboards and transactional inventories
Capacity and cost planning for peak concurrent users

units.title: Operations and project
topics: Telemetry, logging and tracing netcode problems in production
Load testing with bots and soak tests
Protocol versioning, backwards compatibility and live patching
Project: a two-player authoritative game with prediction, interpolation and lag compensation

schedule.title: Architectures for online play
schedule.exercise: Compare client-server and peer-to-peer designs for a four-player card game, a 16-player shooter and a 4-player kart racer, and pick tick rates with reasons.

tasks.title: Build a star topology with one server and four clients, send state updates and count the packets each node sends and receives per second
Write a fixed-timestep game loop that decouples simulation at 30 Hz from rendering, and show it stays deterministic across runs with the same input
Model a four-player peer-to-peer mesh and compare its total traffic and per-node upload with a client-server layout as player count grows to 16

schedule.title: Sockets and the network budget
schedule.exercise: Calculate monthly data use for a mobile game sending 20 snapshots per second of 200 bytes, and decide how far the rate must drop to fit a 500 MB bundle.

tasks.title: Write a UDP echo client and server that exchange 100 numbered packets on loopback and report the number received and the order
Compute bytes per second for several snapshot sizes and rates with headers included and find the largest payload below a 1200-byte MTU
Set a cellular link with 200 ms delay and 3 percent loss in the simulator, run a game stream and judge playability against a data budget

schedule.title: TCP, UDP and acknowledgements
schedule.exercise: Explain why a lost TCP segment stalls later position updates, then sketch the header of a UDP packet that carries a sequence number and an acknowledgement bitfield.

tasks.title: Send a position stream over a lossy link with TCP and with UDP, record the worst gap between updates and explain head-of-line blocking
Implement sequence numbers and a 32-bit acknowledgement bitfield in a UDP sender and receiver and verify which packets are acknowledged under 10 percent loss
Add retransmission with a smoothed round-trip estimate to the reliability layer and measure delivery of 1000 reliable messages at 20 percent loss

schedule.title: Channels, congestion and compact encoding
schedule.exercise: Pack a player state of position, rotation and health into the fewest bits you can with quantisation, and calculate the saving against a naive JSON message.

tasks.title: Quantise a position to centimetre precision within a 1000 m map, bit-pack it with a health value, and check the maximum decoding error
Implement a reliable-ordered and an unreliable-sequenced channel on one connection and show that stale unreliable packets are dropped but chat is not
Ramp up send rate on a bottleneck link, observe loss and queueing delay, then add a simple congestion-aware rate limiter and compare latency

schedule.title: Lockstep and snapshots
schedule.exercise: For a strategy game with 200 units, compare the bandwidth of lockstep (inputs only) with snapshots of all units, and list what must be deterministic for lockstep to work.

tasks.title: Simulate two lockstep clients with an input delay of 3 ticks and show their states match after 300 ticks using identical inputs
Send full snapshots at 20 Hz, then convert to delta snapshots against an acknowledged baseline and report the bytes saved on a 50-entity world
Introduce a floating-point order difference between two lockstep clients, detect the desync with state hashes, and fix it with fixed-point maths

schedule.title: Interpolation, replication and relevancy
schedule.exercise: Decide which entities in a battle-royale map each player must receive each tick and design a priority scheme so a bandwidth cap is never exceeded.

tasks.title: Render a remote player by interpolating between two snapshots 100 ms behind real time and plot the smoothed path against the raw updates
Implement a priority accumulator that fills a 1000-byte packet with the most urgent entities each tick and measure the update age of far objects
Add a grid-based area-of-interest filter to a 200-player world and measure the bandwidth drop against sending everything to everyone

schedule.title: Latency, jitter and lag compensation
schedule.exercise: Explain with a timeline why a player with 150 ms ping fires at a target that has already moved, then work out how far the server must rewind to count the hit.

tasks.title: Measure round-trip time and jitter on a link with 80 ms delay and 20 ms variation by sending 200 probes and plot the distribution
Choose an interpolation delay as two snapshot intervals plus jitter, and show smoothness improves as the delay grows from 0 to 150 ms
Implement server-side rewind that stores 1 second of positions and test that a shot fired at 120 ms ping is judged against the target's past position

schedule.title: Prediction, reconciliation and rollback
schedule.exercise: Walk through a timeline in which a client predicts five moves, the server rejects the third because of a wall, and the client replays the remaining inputs from the corrected state.

tasks.title: Implement client-side prediction with numbered inputs and reconciliation that replays unacknowledged commands after each server state, and count corrections
Blend a prediction error over 100 ms instead of snapping and compare the visible position jump with and without smoothing
Build a two-player fighting-game rollback loop with 4 frames of input delay and measure how many frames are re-simulated at 100 ms latency

schedule.title: Server authority, cheats and secure connections
schedule.exercise: Write a threat model for an online racing game listing five cheats, the system component each attacks and the server-side check that stops it.

tasks.title: Add server-side validation for maximum speed and fire rate to a movement server and prove a modified client sending 3x speed is rejected
Show how a spoofed source address could turn a small connect request into a large reply, then limit it with a token handshake
Detect an aimbot in logged shot data by computing the headshot rate and angular snap speed per player and flagging outliers statistically

schedule.title: Matchmaking, lobbies and NAT
schedule.exercise: Design a lobby and matchmaking flow for a Ghanaian esports league, with a skill rating that updates after each game and a region choice that limits ping to 80 ms.

tasks.title: Implement an Elo update for 20 games between four players and show how ratings converge to the true skill order
Place two clients behind separate NAT gateways and show a direct connection failing, then succeed with a rendezvous server and hole punching
Launch dedicated game-server instances in two regions of a cloud console with an autoscaling rule on player count, and test a surge of players

schedule.title: Persistent worlds, storage and cost
schedule.exercise: Partition a persistent world into four shards, design the inventory transaction that moves an item between players safely and estimate the monthly server bill for 5000 peak players.

tasks.title: Split a 2D world into a grid of shards and hand an entity across a border without duplicating or dropping it, verifying with a log
Write the SQL transaction for trading an item between two players with a rollback on a failed payment, and test concurrent trades
Estimate hourly and monthly cost for a fleet that follows a daily player curve and find the instance size that keeps cost below a given budget

schedule.title: Telemetry, load tests and live updates
schedule.exercise: Plan a load test with 500 bot clients, define the metrics and pass limits, and write a versioning rule that lets a patched server accept the previous client for two weeks.

tasks.title: Instrument a game server to log tick duration, packets per client and dropped inputs, and chart the three metrics over a 5-minute match
Run 200 scripted bot clients against a game server and find the player count at which tick time exceeds its budget
Add a protocol version field and negotiation so old and new clients can both join a server, and test a mismatch is refused politely

schedule.title: Project demonstration
schedule.exercise: Demonstrate a two-player authoritative game on an emulated 150 ms, 5 percent loss link, show prediction and lag compensation working and report measured correction rates.

tasks.title: Build the two-player game with an authoritative server and prediction, and record the number of corrections per minute at 50 and 150 ms latency
Test the finished game under three network profiles (fibre, 4G, congested 3G) and tabulate input latency, packet loss and playability for each
Profile the project's bandwidth and fix the largest cost with delta compression, relevancy or a lower send rate, showing before and after figures
